children: Bitcoin ended the week of September 20, 2026 at $81,159, crossing above its 50-week moving average of roughly $78,788. That 3% buffer above the line may not sound dramatic, but it closes the book on a 45-week period in which Bitcoin traded below one of the most closely watched trend indicators in the market.
The last time Bitcoin managed a weekly close above this level was November 9, 2025.

The catalyst for the breakout was a 6% single-day surge on September 18, which briefly pushed Bitcoin past $81,200. The move was accompanied by heightened whale activity and a wave of short liquidations.
In the days following the September 20 close, Bitcoin traded in a tight range between $81,000 and $81,450.

To put the road here in perspective: Bitcoin hit a cycle low of approximately $58,525 on June 30, 2026. That represented a 53% drawdown from the October 2025 peak above $124,000. The September 20 close means Bitcoin has recovered roughly 39% from that bottom in fewer than three months.

Galaxy Research head Alex Thorn has tracked what happens historically when Bitcoin reclaims this level after a bear-market breakdown. The data covers 13 comparable instances. In 11 of those 13 cases, the reclaim did not result in new cycle lows.
The exceptions matter too. Two of those 13 reclaims did eventually give way to new lows.
Prior episodes that followed the same pattern include recoveries in 2015, 2019, and 2023.

The immediate question for anyone tracking this development is whether Bitcoin can hold above $78,788 on subsequent weekly closes. One week above the moving average is a signal. Consecutive weeks above it start to look like confirmation.

title: Bitcoin closes above 50-week moving average for first time since November 2025
